title: Print Uniform Block Spacing
description: Fix inconsistent vertical spacing between chapters, sections, paragraphs, windows, and other block elements in print LaTeX. All inter-block gaps must use exactly one spacing unit (semio@spacing@single).
summary: Replaced the previous deliberate 2×/1× before/after heading skip with a single, uniform spacing unit across the entire print body: paragraph<->paragraph, paragraph<->window, window<->window, heading<->anything, and nested (SemioNest) blocks now all get exactly one gap (\parskip = \semio@spacing@single). Mechanism: \parskip carries the unit for every paragraph-adjacent junction; every block emits one \addvspace-based before-space that max-merges instead of stacking and vanishes at page tops; nothing emits an explicit after-space (tcolorbox after-skip + the next paragraph's \parskip supply it instead). KOMA's own heading skip is neutralized to 1sp (its beforeskip is suppressed under @nobreak for stacked headings, so the real before-space is now driven unconditionally from \semio@koma@heading@lines). Found and fixed two unshielded \noindent call sites (window header muted-use, kind-window begin) that were harmless at \parskip=0pt but would have doubled the gap now that \parskip carries the unit. Verified with a ticket-local fixture exercising all adjacencies (visually uniform, page-top flush) and a full build: the 5 non-report print/ templates and the real mit-bestand/bericht zwischenbericht (the document from the dev's screenshot) all build clean and render with uniform spacing. The `report` template still fails on an unrelated, pre-existing WIP bug in anchor-aware image-cover-crop code already present in the working tree before this ticket reopened — confirmed unrelated via git diff, not touched here.
